name: Ageospatial
long_description:
Ageospatial helps organizations value the risk on their physical assets (properties, land, infrastructure) remotely using satellite imagery.

97% of commercial properties are never physically inspected because it's too slow and expensive. So insurers price risk based on what the client or broker tells them, and about half the time at least one of those records is wrong. The result is mispricing, fraud, and an estimated $36B in premium leakage every year in the US alone, which gets exposed the moment a disaster hits.

Upload a list of addresses and their GeoAI reads satellite and street-level imagery, maps, real-time data, public records and the insurer's own data to determine what's really there, which natural and human hazards surround it, what changed over time, and which properties are worth inspecting. Each property becomes a living record that underwriting, claims and pricing teams can trace from past to present. Ageospatial deploys inside carriers and MGAs as an AI-native service, so insurers get outcomes delivered.
one_liner: Physical intelligence for every decision with Geospatial AI.

launches.title: Ageospatial - pricing the risk of every property, infrastructure and land on Earth from satellites
launches.tagline: know the assets that you insure in the physical world
launches.body:
**TL;DR: insurers cover buildings, land and infrastructure they've never seen. we look at every one of them from space and tell them what they're really insuring and how risky it is.**

<https://youtu.be/IoGyUfGMV94>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116579&key=user_uploads/2973429/b3467b52-ec9a-41b2-881c-6f84b0f0ba29)

**the problem**

* 97% of commercial properties are never inspected. it's too slow and too expensive to send someone.
* so insurers rely on what they're told such as forms filled in by owners and brokers and half the time, at least one detail is wrong.
* wrong info means wrong prices, fraud, and money lost. insured disaster losses passed $100B in 2025. in the US alone, insurers lose $36B a year to underpriced policies.

**how it works**

* give us a list of addresses, type one in, or click anywhere on the map
* our AI reads satellite images, street-view, maps, public records, internal and live data
* for each asset it tells you: what it really is, what hazards surround it, what changed, and whether it's worth inspecting
* every asset gets a record that updates over time, and those records make the AI better at finding other risky ones
* we set it up inside the insurer’s systems with our own engineers, so they get outcomes without hiring anyone

**who am I** [@Maaz Sheikh](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2973429)

* I've been obsessed with maps since I was 6. I can draw the world map from memory
* I was top 100 globally on GeoGuessr
* modded video games and added location data to them as a teen, made money on mods
* went to college at 17, studied Geomatics Engineering (CS + Geography)
* hired at 19 to support decisions during wars and disasters using satellite imagery, worked on some of the largest crises of our time
* went to the arctic to see if we can grow food where permafrost melts using drone imagery, lived in a container at -22°F
* freelanced for large clients in insurance, energy and government

[ageospatial.com](http://ageospatial.com)
